title: New widget: infiniteHits
body:
Based on proposal in #317.

We could provide an `infiniteHits` widget, based on the default `Hits` that will allow the user infinite scrolling.
- We first display the `n` first results (taken from `hitsPerPage`), wrapped in their own DOM element
- We detect when the user is scrolling a tiny bit before the last results
- We fetch the next page of results and display it (in its own new wrapper DOM element) below the first one
- Whenever the user updates its query string or its filters, we jump back to the top of the page

The tricky part will be to accurately know when we need to clear the list and jump back on top.

I also guess we'll need to tell users that this should not be used in conjunction with the pagination widgets (this will yield to weird UI and results).

comments.body: Also to consider: after scrolling down to the Nth page, if I share the URL of the search page; I want it to load the N pages if I open the URL in a new tab.
